items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I asked him if he would be interested to make a record with me for Pathe-Marconi... we made a nice album titled: 'Together at last'.

ctx.x: May and June 1968 were bad concerning work. Paris was having a revolution and there was a general strike. Every gig, concert and job were cancelled. The Latin quarter was on fire. Police attacked by students were using lacrymator gas. All the clubs were closed. There was no gas for cars, metro and buses were not running. When peace was restored, we still suffered the consequences and hardly worked all summer.
In September, I was engaged for a concert in Antwerp with Ben Webster, Buddy Tate, Jimmy Woody, Wallace Bishop, Milt Buckner and Joe Turner. It was nice to blow with those guys who were all friends.

Then I went to Copenhagen and made a tour with a nice Danish trombone player, John Darville and his group. They were nice musicians and pals and we played Arhus, Holback and did a radio show. Then I went to Oslo, my first time in Norway, and played with a dixieland band, the Big Chief Jazz Band. All were very nice fellows and we had a ball and drank quite a bit.
